t: You're looking at Charity, a sculpture by the French sculptor Jules Dalou, built into a drinking fountain. Dalou was a nineteenth-century artist admired for his perceptiveness and unpretentious realism. The fountain is credited to James Edmeston, who was an architect and surveyor, and also a prolific writer of church hymns. So a figure of charity sits here as a public gift of water, the work of two quite different talents.
